cards.text: Right before this, the book warns a son not to give in when sinners entice him (Proverbs 1:10). Now Wisdom herself calls out, and she's got a message for the simple ones. Grab a seat, friend, because she did NOT come here for small talk.

cards.question: True or false: Wisdom saves her speech for a quiet room where only a few people can hear.

cards.text: Wisdom opens her speech with a question: "How long, O simple ones, will you love your simple ways?" That's the voice of somebody watching you hit snooze for the forty-seventh time.

cards.question: Right after the simple ones, who else does Wisdom call out?
Wisdom keeps asking the simple ones and the scoffers and fools "How long" they'll go on this way. What does that question show?

answers.text: they've ignored her for a long time
she just arrived in their city
she wants to know the time

cards.text: Then Wisdom tells them what could have been, which is the worst kind of news, like finding out the meeting you skipped had free cookies. If they had repented at her rebuke, she says, "then surely I would have poured out my spirit on you…"

cards.question: Wisdom says if they had repented at her rebuke, she would have poured out her spirit on them. What else would she have done?

answers.text: made her words known to them
made them rulers of the city

cards.text: But Wisdom called, and they refused. She held out her hand, and no one took it, which is like reaching down to help somebody up and they just STARE at your hand, except it's EVERYBODY.

cards.question: True or false: Wisdom says they took her counsel and only turned down her correction.

cards.text: Then the tone flips. Wisdom says, "in turn I will mock your calamity; I will sneer when terror strikes you…"
Wisdom says their dread will come like a storm and their destruction like a whirlwind, when distress and anguish overwhelm them.

cards.question: Wisdom says that when distress and anguish overwhelm them, the people will do something. What will they do?
True or false: Wisdom says that when the people earnestly seek her in their trouble, they will find her.

cards.text: So why won't Wisdom answer? She spells it out like a manager reading back every email you never opened, and first on the list: they hated knowledge.

cards.question: True or false: Along with hating knowledge, Wisdom says the people chose not to fear the LORD.

cards.text: Wisdom says they accepted none of her counsel and despised all her reproof. NONE of it, friend, and I thought I was stubborn arguing with my own oven timer.

cards.question: Wisdom says the people will eat the fruit of their own way. What does that mean?

answers.text: they get what their own choices bring
they finally have plenty to eat
someone else pays for their choices

cards.text: Wisdom says they'll be filled with their own devices. Then she says the waywardness of the simple will slay them, and the complacency of fools will destroy them.

cards.question: True or false: Wisdom ends her speech with a promise that whoever listens to her will dwell in safety, secure from the fear of evil.
